title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from this page and the neighbouring ones. Grothendieck works with 'dispositions' (E, ≤, |o|): a preordered set carrying an orthogonality or incompatibility relation |o|. To each disposition E he attaches Σ_E, a set of saturated (bi-orthogonally closed) subsets of E. Σ_E is a complete lattice with an orthocomplement C, where ξ|o|η means η ≤ C(ξ). The abstract objects Σ of this kind are what the page calls (something like) 'partitions'.

Prop. 2 (on an earlier page) gives conditions a), b) on a map σ: E → Σ that make Σ canonically isomorphic to Σ_E. The isomorphism uses two maps:
- β(S) = {x ∈ E : σ(x) ≤ S}, going from Σ to Σ_E;
- α(A) = Sup σ(A), going back.

This page finishes a proposition with five equivalent conditions (i)–(v):
- (i), and its variants (iv), (v), imply (ii) and (iii). This comes from the constructions of β and α in Prop. 2.
- (iii) implies (i) immediately; it essentially needs only the surjectivity of a map τ.
- (ii) implies (i) is reduced to a corollary, applied to the canonical map E → Σ_E.

Corollary. Let E be a disposition, Σ a complete orthocomplemented 'partition' object, and σ: E → Σ a map. Assume a). Then condition b) of Prop. 2 is equivalent to:
- b') β maps Σ into Σ_E and is injective. (He first wrote 'bijective', then corrected it to 'injective'.)

Proof of b') ⇒ b). Fix S in Σ and put S' = Sup σ(β(S)). Then S' ≤ S, so β(S') ⊆ β(S). Conversely, every x in β(S) satisfies σ(x) ≤ S', so β(S) ⊆ β(S'). Hence β(S) = β(S'), and injectivity of β gives S = S'.

So every element of Σ is the join of the σ-images below it: σ(E) is join-dense in Σ, which is presumably the content of b).

The surrounding pages give the context. The previous page has a density lemma (sup testing against a dense subset). The next page has Corollary 5: a dense E' ⊆ E gives Σ_{E'} ≅ Σ_E via A ↦ A ∩ E' and its inverse. This is the analogue of the forcing fact that a dense subposet has the same regular-open (Boolean) completion. Overall the page belongs to a characterisation of the canonical completion Σ_E by a universal or density property, in the style of the MacNeille or Boolean completion.
errors: No mathematical error found. The b') ⇒ b) argument is correct and short.
The 'bijective' → 'injective' correction is right: only injectivity is used, and surjectivity onto Σ_E is not needed for this implication.

ideas.what: Characterising when a map σ: E → Σ into a complete orthocomplemented lattice identifies Σ with the canonical completion Σ_E, via join-density of σ(E) (S = Sup σ(β(S))) and injectivity of S ↦ β(S).
ideas.modern_name: Uniqueness / characterisation of the completion of a poset by join-density: MacNeille completion; Boolean (regular-open) completion of a separative poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacNeille (1937); Boolean completion of posets in forcing (Cohen, Scott, Solovay, 1960s)

ideas.what: A dense subset of a disposition has the same completion Σ (context from adjacent pages).
ideas.modern_name: A dense subposet has an isomorphic regular-open algebra, RO(D) ≅ RO(P)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine step in an order-theoretic completion argument. It is essentially the join-density characterisation of the MacNeille/Boolean completion, rederived in Grothendieck's own vocabulary of 'dispositions'. It is of biographical interest only, showing him working on orthogonality and completion structures in 1986.
transcription_corrections: Line 4 is probably '(iv),(v)) impliquent (ii),(iii) ...'; the parenthetical remark that follows is illegible, and 'jusqu'ici pas faits' is doubtful.
'Cela équivaut au corollaire suivant, appliqué à : E → Σ_E' rather than '...[?] que'.
The corollary begins 'Soient E une disposition, Σ une [?] partition(s)', not 'E un ensemble'.
'(et simplement la surjectivité de τ)' is legible as written.
'S' = Sup σ(β(S)) ≤ S': the scribbled-out symbols around it are cancelled marks, not part of the formula.
'On a vu dans la démonstration que b) ⇒ b')' (the demonstration of Prop. 2).
